scope: User-requested further research into seed + substring offset + structured residual. Literature review, mathematical analysis and one finite exhaustive counting demonstration only.
hypothesis: A selected generated substring can expose a compressible residual, including a structured residual with half its bits set. Complete selection and correction costs determine whether it saves bits.

fixed_demo.targets: Every one of the 4096 possible inputs; no sampling or corpus access
fixed_demo.generator: SHA-256(b'CIX-seed-offset-toy-v1:' + one-byte seed), bits most significant first
fixed_demo.generated_code: 1-bit generated tag + 2-bit seed + 4-bit offset + 2-bit residual-mask index = 9 bits
fixed_demo.selection: First matching seed/offset/mask in ascending lexicographic order, otherwise raw
fixed_demo.control: Original 12 bits, plus separate counts for matching and nonmatching inputs
fixed_demo.validation: Decode every chosen representation from its bits using the shared fixed specification; confirm unique codewords and prefix-code Kraft sum
fixed_demo.excluded_costs: Input length, format identifier, byte alignment and archive framing are fixed or omitted; these favorable toy assumptions are explicit, not a physical CIX archive claim

interpretation: A constructed source win validates possibility only. Whole-universe accounting exposes selection advantage. Neither result qualifies a CIX feature or establishes that real archives are incompressible.
release_gate: Unchanged; no corpus reads, benchmark restart, production source changes, dependency acquisition or publication.
